**Definition 3.1** {#def-2 .definition tag=D102 env=definition}

An integer $p > 1$ is prime when its only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$, in the sense of [Definition 2.1](#def-1).

**Theorem 3.2** {#thm-1 .statement tag=T101 env=theorem}

There are infinitely many primes.

**Conjecture 3.3** {#conj-1 .statement tag=C101 env=conjecture}

There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2$ is also prime.

**Example 3.4** {#ex-1 .example tag=X101 env=example}

The pairs $(3, 5)$, $(5, 7)$ and $(11, 13)$ are of the form in [Conjecture 3.3](#conj-1).

**Corollary 3.5** {#cor-1 .statement tag=K101 env=corollary}

For each $N$ there is a prime $p$ with $p > N$.

**Proof.** {#proof-3 .proof tag=P103}

This is a restatement of [Theorem 3.2](#thm-1). We also use Proposition 2.4 with $m = -1$.
